items.title: 66100_Bud Freeman oral history interview
items.q: We went out that night, went to a little restaurant in the Village

ctx.x: I remember one time, the only time I think he came, unless I am mistaken. I was playing with Benny Goodman and the producer of the show had Panassie Pernasie, John Hammond Panassie. I think, was not the producer -- he got Pernasian to talk and I remember Mezzrow was with him, had come with him to the show.

That was the only time I saw them. We went out that night, went to a little restaurant in the Village, and I remember that a corny recording of Tiger Rag was being played on the Musak, they had in the restaurant, and we were all laughing, it was a satire on jazz, it was so bad, and Panassie Pernasian, he thought it was excellent, so I began to realize that he might not have known too much about jazz.
I think he was very intuitive, but he was very much influenced by Mezz.
